# Command-line reference

This reference is generated from the same Clap definitions used by the `wavlab` executable.

## `wavlab`

```text
Inspect and process PCM WAV files

Usage: wavlab <COMMAND>

Commands:
  sine-wave               Generate a mono sine-wave WAV file
  square-wave             Generate a mono square-wave WAV file directly
  square-wave-additive    Generate a mono square-wave WAV file by additive synthesis
  triangle-wave           Generate a mono triangle-wave WAV file directly
  triangle-wave-additive  Generate a mono triangle-wave WAV file by additive synthesis
  sawtooth-wave           Generate a mono sawtooth-wave WAV file directly
  sawtooth-wave-additive  Generate a mono sawtooth-wave WAV file by additive synthesis
  white-noise             Generate a mono white-noise WAV file
  pink-noise              Generate a mono pink-noise WAV file
  metadata                Load and display a WAV file's metadata
  normalize               Normalize the peak level to 0 dBFS
  normalize-db            Normalize the peak to a specified level in dBFS
  gain                    Multiply every sample by a linear gain factor
  gain-db                 Apply an amplitude gain measured in decibels
  saturate                Apply sigmoid soft clipping that approximates tape saturation
  digital-delay-mono      Apply a clean delay using the same settings for every input channel
  digital-delay-stereo    Apply a clean stereo delay with independent left and right settings
  analog-delay-mono       Apply a low-pass-filtered delay using the same settings for every channel
  analog-delay-stereo     Apply a low-pass-filtered stereo delay with independent channel settings
  tape-delay-mono         Apply a saturated, low-pass-filtered delay to every input channel
  tape-delay-stereo       Apply a saturated stereo delay with independent channel settings
  chorus-mono             Apply chorus using the same LFO settings for every input channel
  chorus-stereo           Apply stereo chorus with independent left and right LFO settings
  vibrato-mono            Apply fully wet chorus as vibrato using the same settings for every channel
  vibrato-stereo          Apply stereo vibrato with independent left and right LFO settings
  flanger-mono            Apply flanging using the same settings for every input channel
  flanger-stereo          Apply stereo flanging with independent left and right settings
  tremolo                 Apply LFO-controlled volume modulation
  autopan                 Apply LFO-controlled panning and always output stereo
  phaser-mono             Apply phasing using the same LFO settings for every input channel
  phaser-stereo           Apply stereo phasing with independent left and right LFO settings
  modulated-filter        Apply an LFO-modulated low-pass or high-pass filter
  reverb                  Apply a classic Schroeder algorithmic reverb
  eq-peak                 Apply a peaking EQ boost or cut around a center frequency
  eq-lowshelf             Apply a low-shelf EQ boost or cut
  eq-highshelf            Apply a high-shelf EQ boost or cut
  eq-allpass              Apply an all-pass filter that changes phase while preserving magnitude
  eq-bandpass             Apply a constant-skirt-gain band-pass filter
  eq-lowpass              Apply a 12 dB-per-octave low-pass filter
  eq-highpass             Apply a 12 dB-per-octave high-pass filter
  reverse                 Reverse the audio while preserving the channel order in each frame
  flip-phase              Invert the polarity of every sample
  swap-channels           Swap the left and right channels of a stereo file
  split-stereo            Split a stereo WAV file into separate mono left and right files
  split-mid-side          Split a stereo WAV file into separate mono mid and side files
  split                   Split a WAV file at one or more millisecond positions
  left-right-to-stereo    Combine separate mono left and right WAV files into stereo
  mid-side-to-stereo      Decode separate mono mid and side WAV files into stereo
  mix                     Mix two or more WAV files starting at the first frame
  join                    Join two or more compatible WAV files end-to-end
  help                    Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -h, --help
          Print help

  -V, --version
          Print version
```

## `wavlab sine-wave`

```text
Generate a mono sine-wave WAV file

Usage: wavlab sine-wave <OUTPUT> <FREQUENCY> <SAMPLE_RATE> <BIT_DEPTH> <LENGTH_MS>

Arguments:
  <OUTPUT>
          Destination WAV file

  <FREQUENCY>
          Frequency in Hz

  <SAMPLE_RATE>
          Output sample rate in Hz

  <BIT_DEPTH>
          Output integer PCM bit depth: 8, 16, 24, or 32

  <LENGTH_MS>
          Output length in milliseconds

Options:
  -h, --help
          Print help
```

## `wavlab square-wave-additive`

```text
Generate a mono square-wave WAV file by additive synthesis

Usage: wavlab square-wave-additive <OUTPUT> <FREQUENCY> <SAMPLE_RATE> <BIT_DEPTH> <LENGTH_MS> [HARMONICS]

Arguments:
  <OUTPUT>
          Destination WAV file

  <FREQUENCY>
          Fundamental frequency in Hz

  <SAMPLE_RATE>
          Output sample rate in Hz

  <BIT_DEPTH>
          Output integer PCM bit depth: 8, 16, 24, or 32

  <LENGTH_MS>
          Output length in milliseconds

  [HARMONICS]
          Maximum odd harmonics to sum; frequencies at or above Nyquist are omitted

          [default: 1000]

Options:
  -h, --help
          Print help
```

## `wavlab normalize`

```text
Normalize the peak level to 0 dBFS

Usage: wavlab normalize <INPUT> [OUTPUT]

Arguments:

          WAV file to process

  [OUTPUT]
          Destination WAV file; defaults to overwriting the input file

          Print help
```

```text
Normalize the peak to a specified level in dBFS

Usage: wavlab normalize-db <INPUT> <TARGET_DB> [OUTPUT]

Arguments:
  <INPUT>
          WAV file to process

  <TARGET_DB>
          Target peak level in dBFS. Positive values may cause clipping

  [OUTPUT]
          Destination WAV file; defaults to overwriting the input file

Options:
  -h, --help
          Print help
```

## `wavlab saturate`

```text
Apply sigmoid soft clipping that approximates tape saturation

Usage: wavlab saturate <INPUT> <DRIVE_DB> [OUTPUT]

Arguments:
  <INPUT>
          WAV file to process

          Destination WAV file; defaults to overwriting the input file

  -h, --help
          Print help
```

## `wavlab digital-delay-mono`

```text
Apply a clean delay using the same settings for every input channel

Usage: wavlab digital-delay-mono [OPTIONS] <INPUT> <DELAY_MS> <FEEDBACK> <MIX> [OUTPUT]

Arguments:
  <INPUT>
          WAV file to process

  <DELAY_MS>
          Delay time in milliseconds; fractional values are supported

  <FEEDBACK>
          Feedback from -1 to 1

  <MIX>
          Wet proportion from 0 (dry) to 1 (wet)

  [OUTPUT]
          Destination WAV file; defaults to overwriting the input file

Options:
      --tail-ms <TAIL_MS>
          Additional output tail in milliseconds

          [default: 0]

  -h, --help
          Print help
```

## `wavlab digital-delay-stereo`

```text
Apply a clean stereo delay with independent left and right settings

Usage: wavlab digital-delay-stereo [OPTIONS] <INPUT> <LEFT_DELAY_MS> <LEFT_FEEDBACK> <RIGHT_DELAY_MS> <RIGHT_FEEDBACK> <MIX> [OUTPUT]

Arguments:
  <INPUT>
          WAV file to process

  <LEFT_DELAY_MS>
          Left-channel delay time in milliseconds; fractional values are supported

  <LEFT_FEEDBACK>
          Left-channel feedback from -1 to 1

  <RIGHT_DELAY_MS>
          Right-channel delay time in milliseconds; fractional values are supported

  <RIGHT_FEEDBACK>
          Right-channel feedback from -1 to 1

  <MIX>
          Wet proportion from 0 (dry) to 1 (wet)

  [OUTPUT]
          Destination WAV file; defaults to overwriting the input file

Options:
      --tail-ms <TAIL_MS>
          Additional output tail in milliseconds

          [default: 0]

  -h, --help
          Print help
```

## `wavlab flanger-mono`

```text
Apply flanging using the same settings for every input channel

Usage: wavlab flanger-mono <INPUT> <DEPTH> <FREQUENCY_HZ> <FEEDBACK> <MIX> [OUTPUT]

Arguments:
  <INPUT>
          WAV file to process

  <DEPTH>
          Normalized depth from 0 (one-sample delay) to 1 (10 ms maximum delay)

  <FREQUENCY_HZ>
          Triangle-LFO frequency in Hz, from 0.1 to 10

  <FEEDBACK>
          Signed feedback from -0.95 to 0.95; negative values avoid the short-delay level boost

  <MIX>
          Wet proportion from 0 (dry) to 1 (wet)

  [OUTPUT]
          Destination WAV file; defaults to overwriting the input file

Options:
  -h, --help
          Print help
```

## `wavlab flanger-stereo`

```text
Apply stereo flanging with independent left and right settings

Usage: wavlab flanger-stereo <INPUT> <LEFT_DEPTH> <LEFT_FREQUENCY_HZ> <LEFT_FEEDBACK> <RIGHT_DEPTH> <RIGHT_FREQUENCY_HZ> <RIGHT_FEEDBACK> <MIX> [OUTPUT]

Arguments:
  <INPUT>
          WAV file to process

  <LEFT_DEPTH>
          Normalized left-channel depth from 0 to 1

  <LEFT_FREQUENCY_HZ>
          Left triangle-LFO frequency in Hz, from 0.1 to 10

  <LEFT_FEEDBACK>
          Signed left feedback from -0.95 to 0.95; negative values reduce short-delay level boosts

  <RIGHT_DEPTH>
          Normalized right-channel depth from 0 to 1

  <RIGHT_FREQUENCY_HZ>
          Right triangle-LFO frequency in Hz, from 0.1 to 10

  <RIGHT_FEEDBACK>
          Signed right feedback from -0.95 to 0.95; negative values reduce short-delay level boosts

  <MIX>
          Wet proportion from 0 (dry) to 1 (wet)

  [OUTPUT]
          Destination WAV file; defaults to overwriting the input file

Options:
  -h, --help
          Print help
```

## `wavlab tremolo`

```text
Apply LFO-controlled volume modulation

Usage: wavlab tremolo <INPUT> <DEPTH> <FREQUENCY_HZ> <WAVEFORM> [OUTPUT]

Arguments:
  <INPUT>
          WAV file to process

  <DEPTH>
          Modulation depth from 0 (unchanged) to 1 (full range)

  <FREQUENCY_HZ>
          LFO frequency in Hz

  <WAVEFORM>
          LFO waveform

          Possible values:
          - sine:     Sine wave
          - triangle: Triangle wave
          - square:   Square wave

  [OUTPUT]
          Destination WAV file; defaults to overwriting the input file

Options:
  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

## `wavlab phaser-mono`

```text
Apply phasing using the same LFO settings for every input channel

Usage: wavlab phaser-mono [OPTIONS] <INPUT> <DEPTH> <FREQUENCY_HZ> <CENTER_FREQUENCY_HZ> <WAVEFORM> <MIX> [OUTPUT]

Arguments:
  <INPUT>
          WAV file to process

  <DEPTH>
          Normalized sweep depth from 0 (fixed center) to 1 (plus or minus two octaves)

  <FREQUENCY_HZ>
          LFO frequency in Hz

  <CENTER_FREQUENCY_HZ>
          Center frequency of the sweep, in Hz

  <WAVEFORM>
          LFO waveform

          Possible values:
          - sine:     Sine wave
          - triangle: Triangle wave
          - square:   Square wave

  <MIX>
          Wet proportion from 0 (dry) to 1 (wet); 0.5 produces the strongest notches

  [OUTPUT]
          Destination WAV file; defaults to overwriting the input file

Options:
      --stages <STAGES>
          Number of second-order all-pass filters connected in series

          [default: 3]

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

## `wavlab phaser-stereo`

```text
Apply stereo phasing with independent left and right LFO settings

Usage: wavlab phaser-stereo [OPTIONS] <INPUT> <LEFT_DEPTH> <LEFT_FREQUENCY_HZ> <LEFT_CENTER_FREQUENCY_HZ> <LEFT_WAVEFORM> <RIGHT_DEPTH> <RIGHT_FREQUENCY_HZ> <RIGHT_CENTER_FREQUENCY_HZ> <RIGHT_WAVEFORM> <MIX> [OUTPUT]

Arguments:
  <INPUT>
          WAV file to process

  <LEFT_DEPTH>
          Normalized left-channel sweep depth from 0 to 1

  <LEFT_FREQUENCY_HZ>
          Left-channel LFO frequency in Hz

  <LEFT_CENTER_FREQUENCY_HZ>
          Left-channel center frequency in Hz

  <LEFT_WAVEFORM>
          Left-channel LFO waveform

          Possible values:
          - sine:     Sine wave
          - triangle: Triangle wave
          - square:   Square wave

  <RIGHT_DEPTH>
          Normalized right-channel sweep depth from 0 to 1

  <RIGHT_FREQUENCY_HZ>
          Right-channel LFO frequency in Hz

  <RIGHT_CENTER_FREQUENCY_HZ>
          Right-channel center frequency in Hz

  <RIGHT_WAVEFORM>
          Right-channel LFO waveform

          Possible values:
          - sine:     Sine wave
          - triangle: Triangle wave
          - square:   Square wave

  <MIX>
          Wet proportion from 0 (dry) to 1 (wet); 0.5 produces the strongest notches

  [OUTPUT]
          Destination WAV file; defaults to overwriting the input file

Options:
      --stages <STAGES>
          Number of second-order all-pass filters connected in series

          [default: 3]

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

## `wavlab modulated-filter`

```text
Apply an LFO-modulated low-pass or high-pass filter

Usage: wavlab modulated-filter <INPUT> <MINIMUM_FREQUENCY_HZ> <MAXIMUM_FREQUENCY_HZ> <FREQUENCY_HZ> <FILTER_TYPE> <WAVEFORM> <Q> [OUTPUT]

Arguments:
  <INPUT>
          WAV file to process

  <MINIMUM_FREQUENCY_HZ>
          Lowest cutoff reached by the sweep, in Hz

  <MAXIMUM_FREQUENCY_HZ>
          Highest cutoff reached by the sweep, in Hz

  <FREQUENCY_HZ>
          LFO frequency in Hz

  <FILTER_TYPE>
          Low-pass or high-pass filter response

          Possible values:
          - low-pass:  Pass frequencies below the moving cutoff
          - high-pass: Pass frequencies above the moving cutoff

  <WAVEFORM>
          LFO waveform

          Possible values:
          - sine:     Sine wave
          - triangle: Triangle wave
          - square:   Square wave

  <Q>
          Filter Q controlling resonance around the moving cutoff

  [OUTPUT]
          Destination WAV file; defaults to overwriting the input file

Options:
  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

## `wavlab reverb`

```text
Apply a classic Schroeder algorithmic reverb

Usage: wavlab reverb [OPTIONS] <INPUT> <ROOM_SIZE> <DECAY_SECONDS> <MIX> [OUTPUT]

Arguments:
  <INPUT>
          WAV file to process

  <ROOM_SIZE>
          Normalized room size from 0 (small) to 1 (large)

  <DECAY_SECONDS>
          RT60 decay time in seconds

  <MIX>
          Wet proportion from 0 (dry) to 1 (wet)

  [OUTPUT]
          Destination WAV file; defaults to overwriting the input file

Options:
      --tail-ms <TAIL_MS>
          Additional output tail in milliseconds

          [default: 0]

  -h, --help
          Print help
```

## `wavlab eq-peak`

```text
Apply a peaking EQ boost or cut around a center frequency

Usage: wavlab eq-peak <INPUT> <FREQUENCY> <GAIN_DB> <BANDWIDTH> [OUTPUT]

Arguments:
  <INPUT>
          WAV file to process

  <FREQUENCY>
          Center frequency of the affected band, in Hz

  <GAIN_DB>
          Gain at the center frequency, in dB

  <BANDWIDTH>
          Width of the affected band, in octaves

  [OUTPUT]
          Destination WAV file; defaults to overwriting the input file

Options:
  -h, --help
          Print help
```
